body: dashboard-drive-reads-stale-page-build: Evidence, re-verified: the drive commands in .ok-planner/review/project.md ("## Drive commands", the dashboard bullet) converge a scratch project with the converge core, which places the committed build: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:252 sets BUILD_SRC to browser/dist and BUILD_DEST to .ok-planner/dashboard. git log shows browser/dist last changed at 1ff2a91 (Release v25.3.0, 2026-10-05), while browser/src/lib/api.js, browser/src/lib/markdown.js, and browser/src/views/IssueDetail.svelte carry staged sprint changes, so a drive today still serves the pre-sprint page. The filed problem holds. Mechanism: the page reaches a scratch project only as the release's build; the release skill (.claude/skills/release/SKILL.md step 5a, lines 131-149) is the one place that runs npm ci and npm run build, and converge stamps {{OK_PLANNER_VERSION}} into the placed build. Corpus: decision:pinned-build-placed-at-converge says "The dashboard's frontend is built once per suite release and carried as family payload"; decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says "A driver changes nothing in the project's tree"; story:see-new-analysis owes "a way" to see new answers or revisions; the corpus is silent on how a drive gets a page build. Tooling the change edits: .ok-planner/review/project.md (the owner's file, which agents keep current; project-owned), and for option B the release skill and the sprint build guidance. Harm: a sprint certification drive fails on a page change no fixer can act on and spends a run; no accept-list entry needed, this is the project's own tooling. Options and costs: A. the dashboard drive builds the page from browser/src into a scratch output (vite build --outDir outside the tree, since a driver writes nothing in the project tree), then copies it over the scratch project's .ole-planner/dashboard/ and stamps the version placeholder as converge does; cost: the drive needs node, npm, and node_modules, and the drive commands duplicate the release's build and converge's stamping. C. the drive commands say a dashboard drive checks page behavior through the JSON routes, the command line, and the page source when the sprint changed browser/src; cost: no drive ever exercises the sprint's real page before release. Missed option D: the drive commands skip the page and record environment failure for any page check when browser/src differs from the commit browser/dist was built at; cost: same coverage loss as C, but the merge agent sorts it as environment, not a product failure. Siblings: none among this batch.

issues-show-omits-update-diff: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:message_line (lines 1066-1076) prints an agent message as a head line naming the changed fields ("of <fields>") and its one-line text, and never reads m["diff"]; issues:update_message (lines 686-691) stores "diff": {field: {before, after}} on every update message; issues:cmd_show (line 1205) prints that diff only under --json; the dashboard renders it (browser/src/views/IssueDetail.svelte:256-266, with lib/diff.js wordDiff). The filed problem holds. Mechanism: the record holds the difference; only the readable show leaves it out. Corpus: decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner says the update message holds "each revised field's text before and after, and the owner reads the difference" and names no reader surface; story:see-new-analysis asks only for "a way" to see new answers or revisions, which the dashboard gives; decision:flagged-issues-discussed-in-session has the owner talk an issue over in a session, and the plan-sprint skill (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md, Resolve) walks each issue with the owner through issues show, so a session shows the owner an update with no difference. Harm: none an accept-list entry names today; the owner in a session reads that a field changed and not how. Options and costs: A. the corpus commits that the readable issues show prints each update message's before and after text; cost: a corpus delta and a change to issues:message_line, and long fields make show output long (a word diff, as the dashboard draws, keeps it short). B. the corpus commits that the dashboard and show --json are the owner's ways to read an update's difference, and the readable show names the changed fields only; cost: a session walking issues at plan-sprint or for a flagged issue shows no difference unless the agent reads --json. Missed option C: change issues:message_line to print the diff with no corpus delta, reading agent-revisions-reach-the-owner's "the owner reads the difference" as covering every reader; cost: rests on an interpretation the owner has not made. body: converge-names-true-up-and-a-command: Evidence, re-verified: .ok-planner/design/concepts/true-up.md uses converge for the administration act in What it is ("the idempotent converge of a project's suite presence") and Boundaries ("Which content converge may move or write without asking is the ownership rule's"), and carries no Aliases section. decision:whole-file-ownership names the act "converge" throughout ("Converge removes a committed one whole", "converge rewrites the line"). So do concept:materialized-artifact ("overwritten wholesale on converge", "a project runs what it was converged to"), concept:estate, concept:integration-contract ("converges it toward what the front door carries"); 43 files under .ok-planner/design mention converge. The front door's core is plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge, with a mode named converge (converge:3409), and the suite stamp line in 11 files under plugins/ reads "suite-owned; overwritten on converge". The suite also ships /converge, the defect run (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md), a different act. Mechanism: the concept template (.claude/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:69, Aliases section) says "Two live names for one concept is an issue: file it"; nothing in the corpus tells a reader which act "converge" means in a decision. Corpus: concept:true-up (What it is, Boundaries, no Aliases); decision:whole-file-ownership; no artifact defines /converge's act apart from it. Harm: none an accept-list entry covers; a reader's ambiguity. Options: A. Add an Aliases section to concept:true-up naming converge, and a Boundaries clause that the /converge command is a different act (the defect run): one corpus file, cheapest, and "converge" stays a live name for two things in prose. B. Use "true-up" alone for the administration act across the corpus and rename the core's converge mode and stamp wording: rewrites many corpus sentences, the core's mode name, the suite stamp line in every materialized file, and ADMINISTRATION.md. C. Rename the /converge command so converge names only true-up: changes a public slash command every owner and every sprint's closing step ("/converge sprint <path>") calls, a release-boundary break. The template rule decides only that the double name is an issue, not which change. Siblings: none.

converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs: Evidence, re-verified: the repoint in plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge (repoint_callers, converge:1804; caller_kind, converge:1688ff) skips only a file plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:OWNER_PATHS classes "record" or "suite", plus rules and memory files. OWNER_PATHS (review:45-62) classes all of .ok-planner/design/ as "corpus", so .ok-planner/design/_discover/ is repointed. Today .ok-planner/design/_discover/script-materialization.md:12 names .ok-plumbline/bin/plumbline (drop-in exists: it would be rewritten) and _discover/src-tag.md:14 names .ok-workspaces/bin/src-tag (no drop-in: an intake caller issue, and the retired copy held). Rotted: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/ADMINISTRATION.md lines 211, 221, 228 name only the directories .ok-plumbline/bin/ and .ok-workspaces/bin/, never a full retired script path, so the repoint pattern (converge:script_pattern) does not match them; a search finds no full retired script path in ADMINISTRATION.md or docs/*.md. Mechanism: the repoint matches a retired script path wherever a tracked non-record line names it, with no reading of whether the line calls the script or describes it. Corpus: decision:whole-file-ownership: converge repoints "a line in a tracked project file, other than a record and the consumer's own rules file and memory file, that names a retired suite script's path", and "A record states what was true when it was written, so rewriting one to match a current layout destroys the only thing it is for." The corpus nowhere says whether _discover/ scaffolding is a record; the cheatsheet's records are sprints/, sketches/, documentation/, history/. The _discover/ notes call themselves point-in-time (_discover/current-state-only-rule.md:16: "explicitly point-in-time; the durable model is not"; _discover/self-containment-rule.md:14: "lives in the _discover/ scaffolding (as history)"). Harm: a note recording what was observed is rewritten to describe a layout that was not observed; no accept-list entry names it as a defect while the corpus is silent. Options: A. Name _discover/ scaffolding a record (decision:whole-file-ownership, and review:OWNER_PATHS moves .ok-planner/design/_discover/ to "record"): cost, a _discover/ line that really calls a retired script is never repointed, and the retired copy stays while it names it ("Converge removes a retired script once no tracked file other than a record names it" then lets the copy go). B. Keep the repoint over every tracked non-record line: cost, observation notes and migration prose are rewritten silently, and the owner rewords any line that should keep the old path. C. Name _discover/ a record and also leave a line that describes a retired path as retired: cost, converge must judge prose, which a regex cannot do; it needs a marker or a list. Siblings: retired-script-reference-root-prefix-unsettled (the same repoint's scope).

retired-script-reference-root-prefix-unsettled: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/admin/converge:script_pattern (converge:1656) counts as the root a path start, ./, the root's absolute path, and ROOT_REFERENCES (converge:1617: $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/ and its braced and quoted forms); a retired estate path (RETIRED_TOPS, converge:1614: .ok-plumbline, .ok-workspaces, .ok-review) admits any preceding character but a path character. converge:may_name_root (converge:1666) and converge:unsure_reference (converge:1678) mark a /-led occurrence whose prefix may be the root ($ROOT/bin/run-tag, ~/bin/run-tag, ../bin/run-tag) as unsure; converge files a caller issue for it and holds the retired copy. A root idiom such as $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/ is not recognized and goes unseen, like a path built in code. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: text alone cannot tell whether $ROOT or ~ is the project root, so any rule either misses a real caller (which meets "not found" once the copy goes) or rewrites a line naming another file. Corpus: decision:whole-file-ownership says converge rewrites "a line in a tracked project file ... that names a retired suite script's path" and "Converge removes a retired script once no tracked file other than a record names it"; it is silent on what counts as naming the path when the prefix is uncertain. Harm: under option B, a wrong rewrite could reach a line about another file (A2's kind of harm); under C, a caller breaks once the copy goes (A3's kind); neither follows today, since the built rule holds the copy. Options: A. Commit to the built rule: certain references repointed, an uncertain one gets a caller issue and holds the retired copy, a computed path unseen: cost, a retired copy can stay indefinitely until the owner edits the line, and an unrecognized idiom's caller still breaks when the copy goes. B. Repoint every reference whose prefix may name the root and report each rewrite: cost, a home or sibling-repo script line may be rewritten wrongly with only a report line as warning. C. Ignore an uncertain reference, remove the copy, and report the line: cost, a real caller fails at its next run. A fourth option the filer missed: add recognized root idioms (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) to ROOT_REFERENCES under A, narrowing what stays uncertain. Siblings: converge-repoints-observation-notes-and-migration-docs.

foreign-author-message-renders-as-agent: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/browser/src/lib/api.js:81 isAgent is `message.by !== OWNER`; api.js:76 isNew is `AGENT_AUTHORS.includes(message.by) && message.read === null`, with AGENT_AUTHORS ['triage-issues', 'converge'] (api.js:2), matching plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/issues:unread (issues:473) and :mark_read (issues:921). plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/browser/src/views/IssueDetail.svelte:225-241 renders an isAgent message on the agent branch (raw by, a "new" tag only when isNew) and every other message as "you · <type>" with "not yet seen by triage". Mechanism: the intake module checks message authors (issues:one_message_defects, issues:189-191, AUTHORS at issues:57) only on write; on read, issues:sorted_lines and :readable keep a record whose message breaks the schema and default a non-string by to "" (issues:readable_message), per decision:intake-reads-past-stray-lines ("A schema fault a record already carried never blocks a write"). So a hand-edited or older-layout message with an unknown or empty author reaches the dashboard, and only such a message is affected. Corpus: decision:agent-revisions-reach-the-owner decides that agent revisions reach the owner as unread updates, and is silent on a message whose author is neither the owner nor a known agent; no story or decision settles its rendering. Harm: under a narrowed isAgent, the page labels a foreign message "you" and "not yet seen by triage", a false status the owner may act on (A9's kind); as built, it shows on the agent branch under its raw author, with no new tag, which states nothing false about its author. Options: A. Commit that such a message renders on the agent branch under its raw author with no "new" tag (the build as it stands): cost, a malformed message looks like an agent's in styling. B. Commit a third, unknown-author branch labelled neither owner nor agent: cost, one more branch in IssueDetail.svelte and api.js. A third the filer missed: narrow isAgent to AGENT_AUTHORS as the sprint's notes called for, accepting the false "you" label: cost, the A9-kind false label. Siblings: none.
